stem.en: Seismic stations report an undersea earthquake. Which stage of the tsunami warning system comes next?

text.en: Tracking, with coastal tide gauges and radars

feedback.en: Tracking comes third. First the system must find out whether there is a tsunami at all.

text.en: Confirmation, with recorders on the sea floor

feedback.en: Yes. Not every undersea earthquake makes a tsunami, so OBPRs check for tsunami waves.

text.en: Warning Dissemination, by satellite and SMS

feedback.en: Alerts go out in the last stage, after the threat is confirmed and tracked.

text.en: Detection, by a second set of seismic stations

feedback.en: Detection has already happened. The next question is whether a tsunami wave is passing.

explanation.en: The four stages are Detection, Confirmation, Tracking and Warning Dissemination. Not every undersea earthquake makes a tsunami, so after detection the OBPRs on the sea floor check for tsunami waves.

hints.en: Which stage asks whether there is really a wave?
